section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the opening header and date of the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Vayeitzei,
the 9th of Kislev,
the year 5729

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the verse uses the term "one" (echad) rather than "singular" (yachid) for Hashem and Israel.
section.t: "You are One"
"and Your Name is One, and who is like Your people Israel,"
"a unique nation on earth."
And my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, precisely analyzes in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh" of the 9th of Kislev,
that the term "one" (echad) also refers to a numerical one,
[as in "And there was evening and there was morning, one day,"
and afterwards
it is written "a second day," "a third day," etc.],
and since He, blessed be He, is singular and unique, with nothing comparable to Him, and similarly Israel is a unique nation, singular and unparalleled,
it should have said "You are Singular (Yachid) and Your Name is Singular, and who is like Your people Israel, a singular nation."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Israel being a "unique nation" is analogous to an only child, whose love is greater, and questions why the verse says "one nation" rather than "singular nation."
section.t: And he continues in the maamar,
that this—that Israel is a singular nation—is analogous to a father and mother who have only one son, who is called an only son.
For the love of parents for their son, when they have only an only son, is a greater love than the love of parents for their children when they have additional children.
And likewise, the love of an only son for his parents is greater than when there is more than one son.
And so it is also with Israel,
since Israel is an only son to the Singular One of the world,
therefore,
the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel,
and likewise the love of Israel for the Holy One, blessed be He,
is an exceedingly great love.
And he concludes there,
that based on this, one must understand why it is said "and who is like Your people Israel, a unique nation (goy echad)" and not "a singular nation (goy yachid)."
